doc.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000

title: Making the CD and writing 'A Train' with Ray
summary: Ray arranged everything with sidemen; he and Korb rework 'A Train' at the piano.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You know, Plas Johnson, Conte Candoli, Oscar Castro-Neves. It was just awesome. And I think out of that whole thing one of my favorite moments was when Ray, he came down to San Diego to my house, and we’re sitting at the piano going through some tunes and ideas, and we were going to do “A Train.” And he says well my ex-wife used to do stuff — my ex-wife used to take things, you know, and she’d take it slow and then she would make it fast. And so he says well let’s try this with “A Train.” Because I don’t think anybody’s done it. Well we’re sitting there together on the piano bench and he’s playing some chords and it’s just like by the time we got done with doing it slow, we just looked at each other and it was like that’s it. That’s what we’ll do. We don’t need to take it fast. And it was just that moment of creating with him, in such a casual situation. But it was, for me it was just so unbelievable. It was very cool.
